reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - HAHA responses observed indicating immune activation, with 5/24 patients showing positive responses in the 3mg/kg + peptides arm, 2/24 in 10mg/kg + peptides, and 1/24 in 10mg/kg alone. This demonstrates CTLA-4 blockade is occurring. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear evidence of downstream biology changes - high rates of immune-related adverse events (65-80%) across all arms, including serious endocrine and gastrointestinal toxicities characteristic of checkpoint blockade. The irAE profile confirms immune system activation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: This is a Phase I/II safety and immunogenicity study with dual primary endpoints of immune-related adverse events and time to disease relapse. The irAE endpoint was clearly met with high rates observed. However, efficacy data is incomplete - median time to relapse was not reached in any arm, making efficacy assessment inconclusive. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Some dose-response relationship observed in HAHA responses (higher with 3mg/kg + peptides vs other arms), and higher irAE rates with combination therapy vs monotherapy. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This appears to be primarily a safety/immunogenicity study rather than a definitive efficacy trial, with limited efficacy readout.

failure_modes.evidence: Median time to relapse not reached in any arm suggests insufficient follow-up time to assess the efficacy component of the dual primary endpoint, though the safety component was adequately assessed
